core_job: For people who send money to family abroad: type what a provider's quote or receipt says (what you sent, the fee, what they received, the date). The app checks it against the European Central Bank reference rate for that date (Frankfurter, keyless, already in the code) and shows the fee, the margin hidden in the exchange rate, the total cost in money and as a %, and the effective rate. Next to these it shows the World Bank's measured average cost of sending to and from that country (api.worldbank.org SI.RMT.COST.IB.ZS / OB.ZS, curl-verified, e.g. India 2023 1.76%, USA 2023 3.51%) and the UN target of under 3%. Up to 4 quotes can be compared side by side, and each check is saved to an on-device ledger. The converter and rates-table screens, which duplicate CalcMaster, are removed.
signature: Receipt audit. The user logs past transfers from their receipts. Each is re-priced against the ECB rate of its own date, with a band built from the previous, same and next working day's real published rates. The ledger then gives, per year and per corridor: total fees, total margin, median cost % for each provider (from the user's own sends only) and a cost trend (shown only at 6+ sends). The corridor chart shows the user's sends as points at the rate they actually got, so the margin is visible as the gap to the reference line. Competitors were checked through the iTunes Search API, descriptions only (WebSearch is disabled here). The closest is RemitRate (id6780613100): it compares live effective rates and takes affiliate commissions. None of the descriptions read mentions auditing past receipts or showing a World Bank benchmark.
